scientific_name: Phyllophaga spp. and other scarab larvae
traits: Turf lifts like loose carpet — roots are gone
White, C-shaped grub with a brown head, in the top few inches of soil
Two parallel rows of spines on the underside of the last body segment
Armadillos, raccoons, and birds digging at night for an easy meal

look_alikes.difference: White grubs are pale, C-shaped larvae found in soil; June beetles (their adult stage) are brown, oval, hard-shelled beetles that fly at night.
look_alikes.next_photo: A close-up of the specimen — a soft C-shaped grub versus a hard-shelled flying beetle.

copy.what_it_means: Animal digging is usually the first sign — the grubs are the buffet and your lawn is the tablecloth. Fixing the grubs typically sends the diggers looking for better hunting elsewhere.
copy.fact: Animal digging is usually the first sign — the grubs are the buffet, your lawn is the tablecloth.
copy.blurb: Fix the grubs and the diggers leave on their own.

tech_notes: Tug test — roots sheared at grub-damaged spots. Cut-and-peel count per sq ft; treat over threshold per label, water-in required.

traits: Chalk-white to gray weevil with a short snout, about 6-8.5 mm
Leaf edges notched inward from the margin like pinking shears
Drops and plays dead when the branch is bumped
Feeds on a very wide range of ornamentals — over 150 plant species

look_alikes.difference: Sri Lankan weevil is chalky white to gray with a short snout; Diaprepes root weevil has a black wing cover banded with orange or yellow.
look_alikes.next_photo: A close-up from above showing the wing-cover color pattern, next to a coin.

copy.what_it_means: A newer Florida arrival that already feeds on more than 150 plant species — the notched-leaf signature turns up almost everywhere. Cosmetic on mature plants; young or newly planted ornamentals can need protection.
copy.fact: A newer Florida arrival that already feeds on 150+ plant species — the notched-leaf signature is everywhere.
copy.blurb: Cosmetic on mature plants; young ornamentals may need protection.

tech_notes: Confirm leaf-margin notching + play-dead drop behavior. Weevils fly/hide readily, limiting contact-spray success; targeted ornamental treatment on high-value plants.
